segments.text: In the outer asteroid belt there's an asteroid unlike almost any other. It's called sixteen Psyche.
segments.headline: 16 Psyche

segments.text: It's about two hundred twenty kilometers wide.
Most asteroids are rock or ice. But telescopes suggest Psyche is rich in metal.
segments.headline: Made of metal?

segments.text: One idea: it's the core of a baby planet, whose rocky outer layers were smashed away by collisions billions of years ago.
segments.headline: A planet's core?

segments.text: We can never visit Earth's core. It's thousands of kilometers below us. But Psyche might let us see one up close.
segments.headline: A look at a core

segments.text: NASA's Psyche spacecraft launched in October twenty twenty-three. It flies on blue-glowing electric thrusters.
segments.headline: Launched 2023

segments.text: It flew past Mars in May twenty twenty-six for a gravity boost, and is set to arrive in August twenty twenty-nine.
Headlines love to say it's worth quadrillions of dollars. But no one can mine it. The real treasure is knowledge.
segments.headline: The real treasure
